why: Two scripts, 457 lines: reclaim.py reclaims space across the home tree from an operator-approved candidate list, and temp_sweep.py removes scratch directories THIS repository created in the system temp directory. What general cleaners cannot do is the part that makes them safe here: prove a directory is ours before removing it. temp_sweep matches only prefixes this repo creates, verifies each gate-extra directory still has the shape the test fixture produces (a git repo whose only content is a README and optional gate artifacts), quarantines anything that does not match instead of deleting it, and writes an fsynced manifest row BEFORE each action rather than after. A general cleaner deletes by age or by pattern and cannot tell a leaked test fixture from a running installer's working directory. The measured driver: 1,884 directories, 16,279 files, 34,486,913 bytes of gate-extra scratch, leaked one per test run by a cleanup that used shutil.rmtree(ignore_errors=True) and therefore could not fail on Windows read-only git pack files.
what_ours_does: Dry run by default, --execute to act, separate --allow-delete on reclaim.py, a hardcoded never-touch list (claude* session scratch), shape verification before deletion, quarantine rather than delete on mismatch, and an append-only fsynced manifest at state/reclaim-manifest.jsonl. Re-runs its invariants immediately before acting rather than trusting the scan.
strongest_counterargument: Windows Storage Sense is built in, free, already installed, and configurable to clear %TEMP% files older than N days. Had it been enabled, the 1,884 directories would never have accumulated and this tool would have had nothing to do. That is a real indictment: the leak survived because nobody turned on a feature that ships with the operating system. The defence is narrow and it is about EVIDENCE rather than deletion. Storage Sense deletes silently by age and leaves no record of what went, so it would have hidden the defect instead of surfacing it. The 1,884 count is what identified the ignore_errors bug, and an age-based cleaner would have quietly maintained the leak forever at a constant directory count. Deletion is the cheap half; the manifest and the shape check are the half worth 457 lines. If the operator prefers, enabling Storage Sense AND keeping temp_sweep for the audit trail is strictly better than either alone.

alternatives.name: Windows Storage Sense and Disk Cleanup
alternatives.why_not: Built in and would have prevented the entire measured problem, which is why it is listed first. Rejected as a REPLACEMENT rather than as a complement: it deletes by age with no per-path record, so it cannot distinguish our leaked fixture from another program's live scratch, and it produces no evidence that a defect existed. Recommended alongside this tool, not instead of it.

alternatives.name: systemd-tmpfiles and tmpreaper
alternatives.why_not: The Linux equivalent and the better model: a declarative config saying which paths age out and how fast. Directly relevant once the WSL2 migration lands, and it should be adopted there for the Linux side. It does not solve the Windows side today, and it has no concept of verifying that a directory matches an expected shape before removing it.

alternatives.name: BleachBit
alternatives.why_not: Mature, cross-platform, with per-application cleaners and a preview mode that is the same idea as our dry run. Rejected because its unit of work is an application, not a path pattern the operator's own tooling creates, and because it is a GUI-first tool whose CLI is a secondary surface. Adding a 20 MB dependency to delete directories we can enumerate exactly is a bad trade.

alternatives.name: czkawka and rmlint
alternatives.why_not: The right tools for the OTHER half of the operator's request, which is dedup across the home tree rather than scratch removal. czkawka is Rust, actively maintained, and finds duplicates, empty directories and big files by content hash. This record does not claim we should write that ourselves: when the census reaches the dedup stage, czkawka or rmlint is the expected answer and this component should shell out to one rather than grow a hashing pass.

alternatives.name: cargo-sweep and npkill
alternatives.why_not: Ecosystem-specific cleaners for target/ and node_modules/, which are the two largest reclaimable classes in this estate. Complementary and worth adopting per-ecosystem. Neither touches the temp directory or the manifest requirement.

alternatives.name: Do nothing, and fix only the test
alternatives.why_not: The simplest correct option and it is half-right. Fixing tests/test_gate_extra_domains.py to raise when cleanup fails stops the leak at the source and is 25 lines, and it was done first for exactly that reason. It does not remove the 1,884 already on disk, and doing that by hand or by an unrecorded rm is how a deletion happens with no record of what was deleted. The tool exists for the backlog and for the manifest, not for the ongoing prevention.

improvement_owed: temp_sweep measures every eligible directory with a full os.walk before acting, which is wasted work when the answer is 'delete it all anyway'. More importantly it has no selftest and no mutation entry, so it does not meet this repository's own four-layer standard: a tool that DELETES is the last place a missing oracle is acceptable. Owed before it runs again: a selftest that plants a shape-mismatched directory and proves it is quarantined rather than deleted, and a mutation proving that selftest can go red.

evidence.root_cause: tests/test_gate_extra_domains.py used shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True); git marks pack files read-only, rmtree raises PermissionError on Windows, ignore_errors swallowed it, so the cleanup ran on every test and could never fail
evidence.repo_census_effect: a git-repo walk of the home tree reported 1870 repositories before and 28 after, so 98.5 percent of the apparent repository estate was this leak

recheck: Re-run: python tools/reclaim/temp_sweep.py and confirm the eligible count is near zero, which proves the test fix is holding. Then check whether Storage Sense has been enabled, because if it has, the deletion half of this tool is redundant and only the manifest and shape check justify it. Also revisit czkawka for the dedup stage rather than growing a hashing pass here.
